spec.formula: output[c * output_stride/4 + r] = input[r * input_stride/4 + c] for r < block_height, c < block_width (32-bit elements, strides in bytes)
spec.domain: block_width, block_height >= 1; input_stride >= 4*block_width, output_stride >= 4*block_height (any multiple of 4, not necessarily a multiple of 64); pointers 4-byte aligned only
width_bounds: pure data movement: no arithmetic, every output element is one input element
the bytes between block_height*4 and output_stride in each output row (row padding of a sub-tensor view) must stay untouched
reading past the end of an input row is allowed (XNN_OOB_READS) but never writing past an output row
must be correct for every VLEN from 128 to 1024: the upstream 8x8/16x8/32x8 kernels are not (they fail at VLEN 128)

regimes.single: XNNPACK's bench: one call over a whole dense block (up to 1024x1024, 4 MiB each way)
regimes.op32: XNNPACK's transpose operator: 32x32 tiles (edge tiles smaller) with the full-matrix strides
regimes.op32-view: the operator on a sub-tensor view: odd leading dimensions, base pointer offset by one element

measured.cycles_per_element: about 0.5-1.6 for blocks up to 256x256; 13-14 for 1024x1024 (every upstream variant)
measured.memory_forms_e32_m1_cycles: vle32 5, vse32 5, vlse32 16, vsse32 32, vlsseg2/4/8 17/19/32, vssseg2/4/8 16/16/16, vlseg8 32, vsseg8 16 (VLEN 512: 16 elements per register)

candidates.application: the upstream structure: vlsseg<nf>e32 gathers nf columns of VL rows at input_stride, then nf unit-stride vse32 write nf output rows
candidates.expected_gain: parity with upstream; the starting point

candidates.application: mirror the upstream structure: load nf input rows (VL columns each) with unit-stride vle32, write them with one vssseg<nf>e32 at output_stride; segment i is output row (column i) elements r..r+nf-1
candidates.expected_gain: per 128 elements at m1: 8 vle32 (40 cycles) + 1 vssseg8 (16) vs upstream 1 vlsseg8 (32) + 8 vse32 (40); with larger LMUL on the load side the store side dominates less
preconditions: nf * LMUL <= 8 for the segment store
column tails: vl covers columns, nf covers rows (tail rows need a smaller nf)

candidates.application: longer unit-stride loads or stores per instruction: vle32 m4 moves 64 elements in 8 cycles vs 16 in 5 at m1
candidates.expected_gain: fewer fixed per-instruction costs on the unit-stride side

candidates.application: for single calls on large blocks (256x256, 1024x1024 with 4096-byte strides) walk sub-blocks (e.g. 32x32 or 64x16) so each 64-byte input line is used for all its 16 columns before eviction
candidates.expected_gain: the 1024x1024 cells run 13-14 cycles/element vs ~1 for blocks that fit: large headroom in 2-4 cells

candidates.title: Unit-stride loads and stores with an in-register transpose
candidates.application: load rows unit-stride, transpose small tiles in registers with vslideup/vslidedown + vmerge or with e64 zip/unzip (vwaddu.vv + vwmaccu.vx to interleave, vnsrl.wx 0/32 to de-interleave), store rows unit-stride; never vrgather (element-serial)
candidates.expected_gain: removes strided forms entirely; pays ALU ops at 2 cycles per LMUL and narrowing at 4
preconditions: tile edges handled with smaller vl

candidates.title: Move 2x2 sub-blocks as 64-bit elements
candidates.application: treat two adjacent u32 as one u64: strided (segment) forms at e64 carry two elements each, halving the element count of the slow side; split pairs with vnsrl.wx by 0 and 32, join with vwaddu/vwmaccu
candidates.expected_gain: strided forms are element-serial (1 element/cycle for vlse32): e64 halves their element count
preconditions: input pairs are 8-byte aligned only sometimes: e64 loads need 8-byte alignment on RVV or they may trap/emulate; check alignment and fall back

candidates.application: issue the next segment load before draining the current one's stores (upstream 8xv2 does this)
candidates.expected_gain: small; the vector unit is decoupled

candidates.application: dispatch once per call on block shape and strides: full 32x32 operator tiles, narrow edge tiles (width or height < 8), and large single calls take different paths
candidates.expected_gain: edge tiles (7x300, 1024x32 sweeps) are a third of the cells; one path tuned for 32x32 is not best for 7-wide
preconditions: predicates on block_width, block_height and strides only, never on data

candidates.application: read vlenb once and size the tile height to VLMAX (16 rows per m1 register at VLEN 512) so one segment op covers a 32-row tile; stays correct at VLEN 128-1024
candidates.expected_gain: the fixed-tile upstream kernels are fast where valid but wrong elsewhere; a VLA kernel with the same shape at VLEN 512 keeps the speed and the correctness

candidates.title: Column/row tails by a shorter vl or nf instead of a switch
candidates.application: replace the switch over block_width % 8 (seven cases of segment ops) with a smaller vl on the VLA dimension and a single smaller-nf path on the other
candidates.expected_gain: less code and fewer branches on edge tiles (op32 cells with widths 7, 13, 21)
preconditions: segment nf is an immediate: one instruction per nf value

candidates.application: compute row/column pointers and byte strides once per call; avoid 8 output pointer increments per tile when one base plus constant offsets works
candidates.expected_gain: small blocks (32x32 operator tiles: ~280 ns) are dominated by setup

candidates.application: an in-register transpose must not use vrgather: 68 cycles at e8m1 on the X280
